elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer (no provision deeming amounts payable by Customer to be liquidated damages)
elements.evidence: Deleted: "shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty" (whole of 13.5 removed by delete_paragraph p0208)
The only penalty/LD characterisation language ("and not a penalty") is removed; nothing else imposes a penalty on Customer in the rendered text

elements.element: No Customer acknowledgement supporting enforceability of such amounts (damages not susceptible of precise determination / reasonable approximation)
elements.evidence: Deleted: "Customer acknowledges that ... damages may not be susceptible of precise determination" and "a reasonable approximation of such damages"

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No cap inserted; the redline contains only a deletion, and the Termination for Convenience Fee/Termination for Cause Fee remain uncapped elsewhere

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No 'sole liquidated amount' language appears; two separate fees (Convenience and Cause) remain defined elsewhere

offending_extra_words: Customer acknowledges that M&I shall suffer a material adverse impact on its business if this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A)
reasons: Preferred level is achieved: the deletion removes both the deeming of the termination fees as liquidated damages and the 'not a penalty' characterisation, so no liquidated damages or penalties are stated to be payable by Customer.

Minimality fails: the operative offence is the second sentence's deeming language ('shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty') plus the 'reasonable approximation' acknowledgement; striking that sentence (or those words) suffices, and a whole-paragraph deletion also removes the neutral first-sentence recital about M&I's business impact.

Intent is preserved: the defined Termination for Convenience Fee and Termination for Cause Fee are established elsewhere, so no undefined term, contradiction or dangling cross-reference is created by removing 13.5.

Note for the record: because the underlying termination fees survive outside 13.5, the fallback cap (3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) is not delivered — consistent with the locked preferred target, but the margin comment's fallback offer is not reflected in operative text.
